claim.expected_behavior: A subject applying the skill reports that threshold=0.8 requires only a fraction 0.8 (80%) of the molecules in the set to contain the common substructure for it to be returned as the MCS, while threshold=1.0 requires all of them.
claim.scope: Semantics of the threshold parameter of RDKit's rdFMCS.FindMCS, as asserted by the skill's Key Concepts and Common Pitfalls sections. Excludes any other FindMCS parameter and excludes the downstream quality of the resulting SAR report.
claim.statement: In an rdFMCS.FindMCS search, threshold=0.8 defines the MCS when 80% of the input molecules contain the candidate substructure, whereas threshold=1.0 requires every molecule to contain it, so 0.8 is more tolerant of outlier structures.

evidence.candidate_limitations: Revision of candidate 88c9b735 after an independent critique found thr-all-open leaked (its stem defined the parameter) and thr-default-choice duplicative of it. Both are removed; the two surviving open/closed cases were kept and three cases now require the subject to supply the fraction semantics itself from a bare FindMCS call. Expected answers are quoted from RDKit's own API/source documentation and from the peer-reviewed TeachOpenCADD T006 talktorial; authoritative for RDKit's documented interface, but the verifier did not execute RDKit. Three of the five expected values are anchored in TeachOpenCADD's reported run output rather than RDKit's own prose. RDKit discussion #5504 questions threshold=1.0 on tiny degenerate inputs; these cases concern ordinary analogue series. Two cases remai [truncated]
evidence.candidate_scope: Tests only what the threshold argument of RDKit's rdFMCS.FindMCS requires of the input set and the consequence the claim draws from it: how many input structures must contain the returned MCS at threshold=0.8 and under the default, and which of two reported MCS results came from the relaxed run. No case states what threshold means in its own stem. Does not test any other FindMCS parameter, MCS algorithm internals, or report generation.

cases.applicability: The claim asserts that threshold=0.8 defines the MCS when 80% of the molecules contain the candidate substructure. The stem now gives only the call and the set size and says nothing about what threshold means, so the subject must supply the fraction-of-the-dataset semantics itself and apply it to 100 molecules. The expected value 80 is quoted from the TeachOpenCADD T006 passage introducing threshold=0.8.
cases.input:
A medicinal-chemistry series of exactly 100 analogues is read into a list called mols. A maximum-common-substructure search is then run in RDKit as:

    mcs = rdFMCS.FindMCS(mols, threshold=0.8)

How many of those 100 analogues must contain the substructure that this call returns as the MCS? Give the minimum number that is guaranteed.

Answer with the number only on the first line of your reply (digits only, no words). You may explain afterwards.
cases.source_quote: It is possible to lower the threshold for the substructure, for example so that the MCS only has to occur in e.g. 80% of the input structures.

cases.applicability: This is the critique's own suggested replacement for the leaked thr-all-open: it presents only a default FindMCS call over a set of stated size and asks how many molecules the returned MCS must be contained in, so the subject must supply both the default threshold value and its meaning. The claim asserts that at threshold=1.0 every molecule must contain the substructure, so the guaranteed count is the whole set. The expected value 145 is quoted from the TeachOpenCADD T006 load step for this exact set; the default-is-1.0-and-matches-all-molecules semantics is anchored in this candidate's RDKit FMCS.h reference, where Threshold is initialised to 1.0 with the inline comment 'match all molecules'.
cases.input:
The file molecule_set_largest_cluster.sdf is read in TeachOpenCADD talktorial T006 and reported as loaded with a set of 145 molecules. Those molecules are then passed to a maximum-common-substructure search with no arguments other than the molecule list:

    mcs1 = rdFMCS.FindMCS(mols)

How many of the 145 input molecules is the substructure returned by this call guaranteed to be contained in?

Answer with the number only on the first line of your reply (digits only, no words). You may explain afterwards.

cases.applicability: This is the critique's own suggested replacement for the duplicative thr-default-choice: the subject must attribute one of two reported results to the run that produced it. It cannot be answered by recalling that 1.0 means all molecules; it requires knowing the direction of the claim's assertion, namely that relaxing the requirement to 80% of the structures lets a substructure that the outliers do not contain qualify, so the relaxed run can return the larger core. Both numbers are given in the stem, so nothing is leaked about which belongs to which run. The expected value 28 is quoted verbatim from TeachOpenCADD T006's reported output for its threshold=0.8 run.
cases.input:
In TeachOpenCADD talktorial T006 the same set of 145 analogues is submitted to rdFMCS.FindMCS twice:

    mcs1 = rdFMCS.FindMCS(mols)
    mcs2 = rdFMCS.FindMCS(mols, threshold=0.8)

The two runs return maximum common substructures of different sizes: one contains 24 atoms and 26 bonds, the other contains 28 atoms and 30 bonds.

How many atoms does the MCS returned by the second call, mcs2, contain?

Answer with the number only on the first line of your reply (digits only, no words). You may explain afterwards.

cases.applicability: Kept unchanged; the independent critique gave this case the verdict counts. The claim is about what threshold requires of the input set. The selected option is the verbatim RDKit API description of MCSParameters.Threshold; the distractors are the verbatim RDKit descriptions of Timeout, MaximizeBonds and CompleteRingsOnly, so each is a real RDKit parameter meaning that is the wrong answer for threshold.
cases.input:
In RDKit's rdFMCS maximum-common-substructure search, what does the Threshold parameter specify?

1. fraction of the dataset that must contain the MCS
2. timeout (in seconds) for the calculation
3. toggles maximizing the number of bonds (instead of the number of atoms)
4. results cannot include partial rings
5. none of these

Answer with the number of the correct option only on the first line of your reply.
options: fraction of the dataset that must contain the MCS
toggles maximizing the number of bonds (instead of the number of atoms)
cases.source_quote: fraction of the dataset that must contain the MCS

cases.applicability: Kept unchanged; the independent critique gave this case the verdict counts. The claim asserts that at threshold=0.8 the MCS need not be contained in all molecules, which is what makes it tolerant of outliers. The selected option is verbatim from TeachOpenCADD T006's discussion of its own threshold=0.8 run; the distractors assert that all molecules must still contain the MCS, or misattribute the parameter to run time.
cases.input:
A set of 145 analogues is submitted to RDKit's rdFMCS.FindMCS twice: once with default settings, and once as FindMCS(mols, threshold=0.8). Which statement correctly describes how the second run treats the individual input molecules?

1. some molecules were now left out due to the set threshold
2. the MCS must still be contained in every input molecule, but rings may be left incomplete
3. the MCS must still be contained in every input molecule, and only the run time is reduced
4. the number of input molecules containing the MCS is unaffected, because threshold sets a limit in seconds
5. none of these

Answer with the number of the correct option only on the first line of your reply.
options: some molecules were now left out due to the set threshold
the MCS must still be contained in every input molecule, but rings may be left incomplete
the MCS must still be contained in every input molecule, and only the run time is reduced
the number of input molecules containing the MCS is unaffected, because threshold sets a limit in seconds
cases.source_quote: some molecules were now left out due to the set threshold

justification.coverage: Five cases, three of them generated open-answer. thr-count-080: a bare threshold=0.8 call over 100 analogues, asking how many must contain the returned MCS (80) — the subject must supply the semantics the previous stem had given away. thr-count-default: a bare default call over the 145-molecule set, asking the guaranteed count (145) — this is the critique's own suggested replacement for the leaked case and tests the threshold=1.0 side of the claim's contrast. thr-relaxed-size: attributing one of TeachOpenCADD's two reported MCS sizes to the relaxed run (28 atoms) — the critique's suggested replacement for the duplicate, turning on the direction of the outlier-tolerance assertion rather than on 1.0 meaning all. thr-meaning-choice and thr-outliers-choice are retained unchanged with the verdict counts: the first discriminates threshold from other real RDKit parameters, the second tests that individual molecules may be left out. The three open cases each turn on a different fact (the 0.8 requirement, the default requirement, the direction of the effect), so the count is not padded by restatement.
justification.oracle_independence: All five expected answers are quoted token-exactly from bytes Python itself retrieved over public HTTPS from sources independent of the skill and of this verifier: the RDKit Python API page for rdkit.Chem.rdFMCS ("fraction of the dataset that must contain the MCS"), the RDKit C++ FMCS.h source listing (Threshold initialised to 1.0 with the inline comment "match all molecules", which anchors the default semantics used by thr-count-default), and the TeachOpenCADD T006 talktorial from the Volkamer Lab, whose own reported run output supplies "Set with 145 molecules loaded.", "MCS2 contains 28 atoms and 30 bonds.", "some molecules were now left out due to the set threshold" and the 80%-of-the-input-structures passage. RDKit is the implementation the skill instructs the user to call, so its documentation and source are the upstream authority for the documented parameter contract. Scoring is entirely by the installed numeric and choice comparators; no AI judgment scores anything and no expected answer is mine.
justification.stronger_grade_considered: A is the ceiling the local policy defines and this revised design meets its case requirements with five in-scope cases and three generated, all expected answers token-exact from Python-retrieved public HTTPS sources, installed comparators and three trials. The previous critique's limiting factor was case independence rather than source authority, and that is precisely what this revision changes: the leaked case is gone, the duplicate is gone, and the two replacements are the ones the critique itself described. I considered accepting the B this design's predecessor settled at, but that grade belonged to a design with only three counting cases and one generated; accepting it now would understate evidence that no longer has those defects. Going beyond A is not defined; observing RDKit execute would change the kind of evidence, not the letter.
justification.tolerance_basis: The three open cases are scored by the installed numeric comparator at the installed absolute tolerance of 0.000001. All three expected values (80, 145, 28) are exact integer counts quoted from documented output, not measurements, so the tolerance only absorbs formatting such as 80 versus 80.0; it cannot admit a neighbouring count. The two closed cases are scored on the 1-based option index taken from the first non-empty line, so no tolerance applies and a number buried in prose scores invalid rather than passing.
justification.uncertainty: The evidence remains documented-semantics evidence: RDKit was not executed, so the oracle establishes the documented contract rather than observed library behaviour, which matches the claim's scope but is worth reading as a limit. Three of five expected values are anchored in TeachOpenCADD's reported output rather than RDKit's own prose, so for those the anchor is one step removed from the implementation; thr-count-default in particular takes its number (145) from the talktorial's load step while the "all molecules" semantics comes from the separate FMCS.h reference. RDKit discussion #5504 questions threshold=1.0 on tiny degenerate inputs, so a subject correct about the documented contract could still meet that edge case in practice. Two cases remain recognition-form, and distractor plausibility is my assertion rather than a measured property. thr-relaxed-size gives both reported sizes in the stem, so a subject could in principle guess between two options.

prior_objections: thr-all-open is leaked: the stem supplies the exact semantics the claim asserts ('the threshold parameter is the fraction of the dataset that must contain the MCS') and then asks for the fraction meaning 'all', which is arithmetic from the stem rather than knowledge of RDKit.
thr-default-choice turns on the same fact as thr-all-open (threshold 1.0 <-> matches all molecules), merely asked from the other direction, so it supplies no independent evidence.

thr-pct-open's stem presupposes that threshold governs the percentage of input structures that must contain the substructure, so the only step left is multiplying 0.8 by 100; it still counts but is much weaker evidence than the justification's 'exact quantitative content of the claim' suggests.

The justification's coverage argument counts cases without weighing independence, and the stronger_grade_considered section defends A solely on source authority and quote exactness while never asking whether the five cases are five distinct tests.

The claim is narrow enough (two documented constants plus one corollary) that five genuinely independent counting cases may not be constructible within scope; the design reaches five by restating one fact and by definition-supplying stems rather than by widening the evidence.

An earlier version's case thr-all-open was not counted (leaked): The stem itself asserts that threshold is 'the fraction of the dataset that must contain the MCS'; given that sentence, the value meaning 'all' is 1.0 by the definition of a fraction, so the answer is readable from the question and requires no knowledge of RDKit. Suggested replacement: A generated case that shows only the FindMCS call with default parameters over a set of a stated size (e.g. 145 analogues) and asks how many of those input molecules the returned MCS is guaranteed to be contained in, with no sentence in the stem describing what threshold means. This stays inside the claim because it probes the same threshold=1.0-requires-every-molecule assertion, but forces the subject to supply the semantics instead of reading them back.

An earlier version's case thr-default-choice was not counted (duplicate): Turns on the same rule as the earlier thr-all-open (threshold 1.0 corresponds to matching all molecules), asked from the opposite direction; a subject who answers one answers the other, so it adds no independent evidence. Suggested replacement: A case built on the two distinct MCS results the TeachOpenCADD T006 talktorial reports for the same 145-molecule set, one from the default run and one from the threshold=0.8 run, asking which returned substructure came from which run. This stays inside the claim because it tests the asserted contrast in outlier tolerance between 1.0 and 0.8, but cannot be answered by recalling that 1.0 means all.

python_checked.note: Python already verified that every expected answer is quoted exactly from the pinned reference bytes. Judge whether that evidence is fit for this claim at the proposed grade. Python counts cases and cannot weigh them: a function name, a scientific value and a fact the claim never states are the same shape once quoted, so whether each case counts is decided here, in case_verdicts. Python then recomputes the ceiling over the cases you count, under rubric.case_requirements, and returns every rejected case with your described replacement to the planner.

rubric.case_replacement: For every case that does not count, describe a case that would test the claim in its place: what it should ask and why that stays inside the claim. Describe it; do not write expected answers.

case_requirements.A: at least 5 counting cases, at least 2 of them generated
case_requirements.B: at least 3 counting cases, at least 1 of them generated
case_requirements.C: at least 3 counting cases of any answer form
case_requirements.answer_form: each case states it: generated means the subject produces the answer (exact, numeric, python); recognised means it picks from listed options (choice). A mixed design can hold both
case_requirements.enforcement: Python recomputes the ceiling over the cases you count and settles the weakest of that, the proposal and your grade. Your grade is your own judgment of the whole design; do not lower it mechanically for the count, which Python already applies.

case_verdicts.beyond_scope: Asks a consequence or fact the claim never states
case_verdicts.counts: Tests what the claim asserts, no less and no more, without giving the answer away
case_verdicts.duplicate: Turns on the same fact or rule as an earlier case in this design, so a subject that answers one will answer the other and it adds no independent evidence. This covers near-copies, such as the same convention asked at another position or the same value from the other side, not only exact repeats. The reason names that earlier case, which keeps its own verdict
case_verdicts.leaked: The answer can be read from the question itself
case_verdicts.naming: Only recites what something is called, for a claim about what it does

criteria: Whether the expected answers are a fit-for-purpose oracle for this exact claim, independent of the submitted skill
Whether the selected cases and trial count cover the claim's stated scope well enough for the proposed grade
Whether the comparison rule, tolerance and stated uncertainty match what the claim actually asserts
Whether a stronger grade was available and was passed over
Whether each concern listed under prior_objections is now answered by this design, unresolved, or does not apply

Whether each case tests exactly what the claim asserts, no less and no more: not only what something is named when the claim is about what it does, and not a consequence or fact the claim never states, which a subject applying the skill could answer only from the base model's own knowledge or not at all

grades.A: Direct validation against an independent oracle, scored without AI judgment
grades.B: External validation on a curated dataset with materially limited coverage
grades.C: Indirect validation: reproducible properties, invariants or agreement, with no adequate direct oracle
grades.D: Documentary assessment of cited sources only
grades.none: The evidence supports no scientific grade

rubric.instruction: Return the strongest grade this evidence actually supports. Do not approve the proposal to be agreeable and do not lower it to be safe.
rubric.prior_objections: Concerns earlier independent reviewers raised about earlier versions of this design. They are given so you can check whether this version answers them. No earlier grade is supplied, and you must not infer one: an objection that is now answered supports nothing against this design.
